Date: Sun, 9 May 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Unexpected post‑renewal invoice — overage details

Jonas,

Hope you had a good weekend. We received the May invoice today and there is a sizable one‑time charge (~$48k) labeled ‘post‑renewal true‑up’. That number is much higher than the delta we expected based on our usage estimates.

Can you share the usage export and the calculations that led to that amount? We renewed on 2027‑04‑01 and scaled capacity mid‑April; our internal teams ran a short burst test the week of 4/18 but nothing that should produce this magnitude of charge.

We need a breakdown (daily token/hr buckets) and a proposed remediation — ideally something that limits the hit to our April/May cash flow since renewal just closed. Please loop in your billing team.

Thanks,
Morgan

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>

Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Unexpected post‑renewal invoice — overage details

Morgan — thanks for the note and for flagging this. Really appreciate the heads up.

Short version: we pulled the per‑day export and there are three contributors to the charge:
- a sustained burst (4/19–4/21) from a test runner in your staging project that bypassed the usual rate cap;
- a small accounting artifact where non‑production traffic during the renewal window was billed at the new post‑renewal rate instead of pro‑rata; and
- a KV cache warm‑up amplification on a model variant that increased token counts for ~24hrs.

I attached the raw usage export (CSV) and a draft credit note proposal. Ben (billing) and Laura (finance) are looped to triage and approve a remediation path.

Proposal from our side:
1) One‑time operational credit of $12,500 to offset the burst and KV warm‑up amplification.
2) Pro‑rata correction on the renewal window billing artifact — we will reissue the invoice showing the corrected line (estimated reduction: $9,800) and offset the remaining balance against the credit.
3) A short-term configuration recommendation (rate cap + extra guardrail) to prevent the staging test from reaching prod capacity again — we can roll this out as a safety rule immediately.

If that sounds reasonable I’ll ask Ben to issue the credit note and Laura to sign off on the invoice reissue. If you need a larger mitigation we can escalate to our sales leadership, but we wanted to propose a pragmatic fix first.

Attachments: lumen_usage_export_may2027.csv, redwood_credit_note_DL-2197.pdf

Thanks,
Jonas Weber
Principal Account Executive – Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.ai

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 11:23:00 -0700
Subject: Approval request: proposed credit and invoice correction (Lumen / DL-2197)

Team — I reviewed Jonas’s notes and the usage export. Quick summary of numbers I calculated:
- Original charge: $48,120
- Estimated pro‑rata billing artifact reduction: $9,760
- Remaining after pro‑rata: $38,360
- Proposed one‑time credit: $12,500
- Net to invoice after credit: $25,860

From a finance perspective I’m comfortable approving the $12,500 credit as a one‑time operational concession for the staging burst + KV warm‑up; it lines up with prior remediation playbooks for burst adjudications. Please proceed with:
1) Ben — generate the credit note and updated invoice; include a short memo line referencing DL‑2197 and the dates (4/18–4/21).
2) Jonas — confirm the guardrail config change is scheduled (I’d like a short note you can attach to the invoice saying the mitigation is implemented).
3) Jonas/Ben — route the corrected invoice + credit note back to Morgan and the Lumen AP inbox.

I’ve copied Ben since he’ll issue the actual documents. If Lumen asks for a bigger concession we should escalate to VP Sales (noted).

Laura Bennett
Director, Finance, Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.ai

Jonas / Laura / Ben — thanks for the quick investigation and the proposed path. The remediation is acceptable to Lumen. We agree to:
- accept the corrected invoice reflecting the pro‑rata billing fix,
- apply the $12,500 Redwood credit against the outstanding balance, and
- receive the short mitigation note describing the guardrail change.

Please send the corrected invoice and the signed credit note to ap@lumenhealth.com and cc me. Once AP has the paperwork we’ll process the net amount on our standard 30‑day terms.

I appreciate the responsiveness — this keeps our renewal momentum intact.

— Morgan
